items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: writing for Bunny Berigan, Artie Shaw, Benny Goodman and other big band leaders.

ctx.x: The fall of 1997 was an eventful time for Ray Conniff as he celebrated his 81st birthday and the release of his 100th album, “I Love Movies.” Ray has become a legend in the music world as an arranger, producer and creator of “a sound.”

His distinctive blend of big band, orchestral and vocal scoring captured the ears of American listeners in the late 1950s and became a familiar sound on radio and home stereos. He started as a trombonist and arranger in the active years of swing, writing for Bunny Berigan, Artie Shaw, Benny Goodman and other big band leaders. His association with Mitch Miller at Columbia Records led to his first records under his own name, and he now places on the top ten all-time album sellers. His six decade career in music is…
Ray currently lives in Los Angeles, and was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 14, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
